title: Galois direction: every primitive solvable subgroup of S_p embeds into AGL(1, p)

problemStatement.formal: For prime $p$, every primitive solvable subgroup $H \le S_p$ embeds into the affine group $\mathrm{AGL}(1, p) = \mathbb{Z}/p\mathbb{Z} \rtimes (\mathbb{Z}/p\mathbb{Z})^\times$: $\exists \varphi : H \to \mathrm{AGL}(1, p)$ injective. The proof uses Sylow's theorem to extract a unique normal Sylow-$p$ subgroup $P \le H$, identifies $P$ as a $p$-cycle in $S_p$, computes the normaliser $N_{S_p}(P) \cong \mathrm{AGL}(1, p)$, and concludes $H \le N_{S_p}(P) \cong \mathrm{AGL}(1, p)$.
problemStatement.plain: Galois's 1832 classification of primitive solvable permutation groups of prime degree: every such group sits inside the affine group AGL(1, p) of order p(p-1). This sub-OQ formalises the structure-theorem half of the parent slug's open question; the forward direction (AGL(1, p) is itself solvable, primitive, faithful) was discharged in the parent slug.
whyMatters: Quantitative complement to the parent slug's qualitative threshold theorem 'S_n solvable iff n ≤ 4': identifies the largest solvable transitive subgroup of S_p as AGL(1, p) of order p(p-1) for prime p.
First Lean formalization of the Galois-direction structure theorem for primitive solvable permutation groups of prime degree. Foundation for any future Frobenius-group infrastructure in Mathlib.

Galois-theoretic completion of the parent OQ-06 forward direction (PR #19071, Docker-verified 1884 jobs): the combined forward + Galois directions yield the full Galois classification of primitive solvable permutation groups of prime degree.

proven: Classical mathematical result (Galois 1832, letter to Chevalier; modern reference Rotman 1995 Theorem 9.11). Standard in every group theory textbook.
